fields.flowNotes:
Six screens on one ruled sheet, numbered in the corner of each box. Checkpoint 1 job: a PG resident in a Kothrud block photographs the paper tiffin bill her kitchen leaves under the door, picks next month's plan, and pays it by UPI before the mess owner starts chasing her on WhatsApp.

1. Home / paste bill. Opens straight here, no login. One line of explanation, then a dashed drop area reading 'drop photo of tiffin bill', then one yellow button, 'Start'. Start reads the bill and goes to 2. The first three seconds are meant to say: give me the photo, I will do the rest.
2. Pick your plan. The plans read off the bill, with a dashed row of the three choices, 'Veg / Non-veg / Jain'. 'Continue' goes to 3.
3. Delivery slot. A dashed box holding a rough map of the PG blocks with the slot windows beside it. 'Confirm slot' goes to 4.
4. Pay - UPI. The amount the bill came to, drawn as 'Rs 1,800 / month', and one button, 'Pay now', which hands off to the UPI app and comes back to 1 on success.
5. Empty state. What screen 1 looks like before anything has been paid: 'no orders yet - add one' and a single 'Add order' button back to 1.
6. Error - payment failed. The UPI hand-off timed out. 'UPI timed out, retry?' with a 'Try again' button that returns to 4 with the amount still filled in, because retyping it is where people give up.

Screen 1 carries the product. The promise is photograph the bill and be done; if 1 is not one drop area and one button, nothing after it matters.
